content: Always listen for repeated questions and answer directly the first time to avoid frustration.
Use SPIN implication questions only after the customer has fully expressed the problem; avoid re-asking.
In-store: always offer a hands-on demo (e.g., show fast charging speed) to build trust.
When customer says 'let's not go backwards', immediately pivot to closing or value anchoring.
For price-sensitive but low-bargaining customers, state the final price clearly and offer a reservation to create urgency.

name: Direct Apology Reset
condition: When customer shows frustration from indirect answers.
example: 'Habibti, forgive me — let me be direct. [Clear answer].'

name: Implication Deep Dive
condition: After customer states a functional pain point, to uncover emotional impact.
example: 'When [pain point] happens, does it affect [emotional/academic outcome]?'

name: Reservation Close
condition: When customer agrees on price and warranty but hesitates.
example: 'Would you like me to reserve one for you today before stock runs out?'

objection: Customer asks repeatedly about battery life after initial answer.
rebuttal_template: I understand you want certainty. Let me show you right here on the device — we can run a video call and see the battery drain in real time. If it doesn't meet 6 hours, I'll personally help you find another option.

objection: Customer asks for extra discount after bundle promotion.
rebuttal_template: Habibti, this bundle already includes the M-Pencil and keyboard cover at a Ramadan price. I can't reduce further, but I can add a free screen protector and case from our stock today. Shall I prepare the package?
Let me show you our warranty card — it lists all local service centers in Doha. You can also scan this QR code to see the nearest one. No need to ship abroad.
